question_text: Find the area enclosed between the curve y = x², the x-axis and the lines x = −1, x = 2.

insider_note: Comparing this with the previous question shows the contrast between even and odd powers at a negative limit — (−1)² is positive but (−1)³ is negative, which changes whether the subtraction becomes an addition.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Set up the area integral
steps.margin_note: First mark. x² ≥ 0 always — confirm this before writing the area as a single unsplit integral.
steps.memory_tip: Any even power of x is never negative — the simplest case of a curve that never crosses the x-axis.
lines: Since x² ≥ 0 for every real x,
the curve never lies below the x-axis
So the required area is A
steps.why: A square is never negative, so y=x² is always at or above the x-axis, and the area under it over any interval is simply the plain definite integral with no sign-splitting.
common_mistakes: Splitting the integral at x=0 unnecessarily, since y=x² never changes sign.
Confusing this with a case where the curve dips below the axis and needs the modulus of the integral.

steps.label: Find the antiderivative
steps.margin_note: Second mark. x³/3 is the antiderivative — a direct application of the power rule.
steps.memory_tip: ∫x² dx = x³/3 — one of the most basic power-rule integrals, worth knowing directly.
steps.why: Integrating x² by the power rule raises the power to 3 and divides by the new power, giving x³/3 as the antiderivative.
common_mistakes: Writing the antiderivative as x³ without dividing by 3.
Confusing the power rule with the rule for integrating x³ instead of x².

steps.label: Apply the limits and simplify
steps.margin_note: Last two marks. (−1)³ = −1 — an odd power keeps the negative sign, unlike the even-power case in the previous question.
steps.memory_tip: 8/3 + 1/3 = 9/3 = 3 — a clean whole-number answer, a useful check that the arithmetic is right.
steps.why: Substituting x=2 gives 8/3, and substituting x=−1 gives (−1)³/3=−1/3; subtracting the negative lower-limit value adds the two fractions, giving 9/3, which simplifies to the whole number 3.
common_mistakes: Computing (−1)³ incorrectly as +1 instead of −1 — an odd power of a negative number stays negative.
Leaving the answer as the unsimplified fraction 9/3 instead of 3.
